observations:
Torah #225 is a short, tightly structured teaching with 5 bechina edges and 10 distinct nodes, yielding 5 raw connected components that reduce to 3 packages after merging. The Torah's argument flows through four main concepts — רֵאָה (lungs), שֵׂכֶל (intellect), בִּטָּחוֹן (trust), צְדָקָה (charity) — connected by eitza (cause-effect) chains, with bechina edges clustered within the שֵׂכֶל domain and the אָדָם/דִּבּוּר domain.

Candidate clusters examined and rejected:

1. BITACHON (trust) as a separate package: בִּטָּחוֹן is a central concept in Torah #225 and appears in multiple eitza edges (ref=225). However, no bechina edge in the dataset connects בִּטָּחוֹן to other nodes in this Torah. The Rebbe presents בִּטָּחוֹן as something produced by שֵׂכֶל (שֵׂכֶל → בִּטָּחוֹן) and as what enables צְדָקָה (בִּטָּחוֹן → צְדָקָה). These are both eitza relationships, not bechina. No independent bechina cluster of 3+ nodes forms around בִּטָּחוֹן in this Torah. The one adjacent bechina (שְׁבָרִים ↔ בִּטָּחוֹן, edge 519) belongs to reference 60, not 225.

2. TZEDAKA (charity) as a separate package: צְדָקָה is the output-concept of the causal chain and appears in multiple eitza edges (ref=225, edges 2550, 2551, 614, 2125, 2129). However, צְדָקָה has no bechina edges at all in Torah #225. Its relationship to אָדָם/דִּבּוּר is eitza ('through tzedaka, speech is made'), not bechina. A package requires bechina edges as its backbone.

3. REAAH / LUNG domain: The lungs (רֵאָה) are the opening concept of the Torah — 'when the lung is complete, thereby the trust is complete' — but the lungs appear only in eitza edges in the dataset for this Torah (edge 2888: רֵאָה → שֵׂכֶל; edge 520: הָרֵאָה בִּשְׁלֵמוּת → הַבִּטָּחוֹן בִּשְׁלֵמוּת). The one bechina connecting to the lung-domain is the Cherubim/wings metaphor (identified in the gap analysis as missing from the dataset), but that connects the lung-wings to the sekhel-candle system and belongs with Package 1, not as a separate domain.

4. NIPPY / TZIPTZUF (bird-call/chirping) domain: The Torah closes with the concept that tziptzuf (raw bird-sound, Kohelet 12:4) can become speech when one has trust and gives tzedaka, and with the story of the Baal Shem Tov hearing speech in the sound of the harp. However, צִפְצוּף and קוֹל are not given their own bechina definitions in the text — they function as the raw material that is transformed by speech (dibbur), making them eitza inputs to Package 2. The verse from Kohelet and the Baal Shem Tov story are homiletical illustrations, not bechina-identifications of new concepts.

Conclusion: Torah #225's three packages are architecturally clean and complete. The teaching has a causal chain of four stations (לוּחַ → שֵׂכֶל → בִּטָּחוֹן → צְדָקָה → דִּבּוּר) linked by eitza, with bechina clusters at the שֵׂכֶל station (Package 1: the intellect-candle metaphor) and the דִּבּוּר station (Package 2: man-as-speech), and a single evil mirror at the failure of the שֵׂכֶל station (Package 3: failing eyes = failing intellect). The good/evil mirror is: Package 1 (עֵינֵי כֹל אֵלֶיךָ יְשַׂבֵּרוּ — eyes trusting through sekhel) mirrors Package 3 (כָּלוּ עֵינַי — eyes failing from lack of sekhel). Package 2 is the culminating positive achievement that the evil package (Package 3) threatens to block by depriving man of his defining speech.
